value.hook: When reviewing registration liveness classes, native-session holds or pane takeover recovery
value.title: Unknown liveness must win refusal precedence

sections.name: body
sections.value:
PR 237 exposed a branch-ordering trap: observing a failed process probe as unknown was correct, but check_native_roster selected NativeSessionHold before checking holders.unknown. A fresh native Copilot conversation sharing a pane with a different native session therefore waited without the E-RS-PANE-HELD takeover recovery command. Preserving the incumbent row was necessary but not sufficient; the refusal type and recovery path were wrong.

Review classification and refusal precedence together. The regression must use a different native Copilot session with normal native-delivery flags and a valid recorded process tuple, inject an adapter error for only that incumbent PID, and assert PaneHeld names the incumbent and its descriptor is unchanged. The earlier missing-PID and remote OMP fixtures never entered the native-session-hold branch and could not catch this bug. The extended native_claim_supersedes_only_a_confirmed_dead_pane_holder now pins this exact case.

The companion take_over_is_for_the_prime_or_the_panes_own_process_and_retires_only_other_records regression distinguishes an asserted prime role from a real current designation and proves that a running foreign holder vetoes the entire takeover before any tombstone, preserving its queued job as well as all candidate rows. Automatic Dead/Recycled retirement remains policy; the explicit takeover live-holder veto is a brake, and explicitly authorized unknown-holder retirement is a separate path.

Both reviewer P2 findings and the live-holder issue were fixed at f62e59ba315e02351a34055dfe5b635782d17481; final reviewer verdict 874fd621a0fc384beb9686a95dccce9f7ef70be2. PM reported merge 88d52a7f and successful live proof. This note adds the refusal-precedence fixture lesson rather than repeating the existing identity-guard or CI-artifact guidance.
